# `Ffi.Js`

[Back to stdlib index](../stdlib.md)

Ipe.Ffi.Js — the raw typed transport across the Ipê↔JS seam (ports).

Ports carry imperative effects and out-of-band data that have no place in the
view tree — custom elements (`Ipe.Ffi.Js.CustomElement.node`) own
visual-in-view; ports own
streaming and programmatic effects. There is no new language construct: a port
is an ordinary `Cmd msg` (outbound) or `Sub msg` (inbound) plus a `sync` cfg
projection, so ports reuse the `Cmd`/`Sub` machinery already present.

One discipline governs every value crossing the seam: a concrete-ADT SEAL — a
closed, declared, monomorphic value type (primitives, records, tuples,
`List`/`Set`/`Maybe`/`Dict`/`Result`, and user ADTs transitively over those).
A function, an effect carrier, a view value, an open row, a type variable, and
— the security tightening — a `Secret` or reserved-sink type may NEVER cross.
The seal is checked fail-closed at compile time on the CONCRETE argument type
(IPE-N0039), the same predicate the `CustomElement down up` boundary uses.

Two closed ADTs, one per direction, are the whole attack surface as a single
auditable object:

  * `JsCmd` — the OUTBOUND published type. Build one and hand it to `send`.
  * `JsMsg` — the INBOUND published type. A NARROW type, deliberately NOT the
    internal `Msg`: the browser is attacker-controlled, so publishing `Msg`
    would hand an attacker every transition the state machine can reach. The
    inbound `case` that folds a `JsMsg` into a `Msg` is EXHAUSTIVE — an
    unhandled inbound variant is a type error, not a silent drop.

`Decoder Value` is REJECTED: the untyped channel cannot be spelled. A payload
that is genuinely opaque is expressed by NAMING it (`type RawJson = RawJson
String`), never left an untyped hole (parse-don't-validate at the boundary).

Trust vs ordering are two orthogonal flags, never conflated:

  * TRUST → decode gate. The far side (browser JS) is always untrusted, so the
    inbound decode gate is ON: every inbound value runs through the total,
    fail-closed, bounded seal decoder; a malformed / oversized / mismatched
    message is DROPPED whole (observable, no partial value, no panic). Keyed on
    trust, never on transport — in-process is not trusted.
  * ORDERING → staleness. Where ordering matters, name the precondition as a
    typed field on the inbound intent (compare-and-swap), not a framework
    version token.

Per-target lowering, one surface: server-driven (the TEA loop runs on the
server, transport is a network stream) and client-WASM (the loop runs in the
browser, transport is in-process) lower differently under the hood but keep an
IDENTICAL developer surface AND an identical JS runtime API (`ipe.send`,
`ipe.onReceive`, `ipe.onSync`). The seal codec is reused byte-identically both
places; there is no second decoder.

A module whose reachable code uses a port discloses the `js-port` capability,
inferred through the same SSOT the other capability axes use.

## `send`

```ipe
send : a -> Cmd msg
```

`send payload` — an outbound one-shot imperative effect, Ipê → JS
(play a sound, fire analytics, hand off to a hand-written JS handler).

`payload` MUST be a seal-legal value type — a plain, closed, concrete value.
A `Secret` or a reserved-sink type is REJECTED fail-closed at compile time
(IPE-N0039): a secret must never cross to JS. The published outbound type is
one closed `JsCmd` ADT so the whole outbound surface is a single auditable
object; per-variant senders (`playChime = Js.send PlayChime`) keep per-effect
ergonomics over the one closed type.

The runtime encodes `payload` with the shared canonical-JSON seal codec and
delivers it to the page's `ipe.onReceive` (server-driven: encode → stream;
client-WASM: direct dispatch, same tick).

## `subscribe`

```ipe
subscribe : Decoder a -> (a -> msg) -> Sub msg
```

`subscribe decoder toMsg` — an inbound intent stream, JS → Ipê, wired in
`subscriptions`. The `decoder` IS the security gate: it is the generated total
decoder for a seal-legal type `a`, run through the fail-closed, bounded seal
decoder on every inbound value. A message that does not decode is DROPPED whole
— no partial value, no panic; the core never sees a raw blob
(parse-don't-validate at the trust boundary).

`Decoder Value` is REJECTED at compile time (IPE-N0039): the untyped channel
cannot be spelled. The decoded `a` should be one closed `JsMsg` ADT — a narrow
published type, NEVER the internal `Msg` — and the `case` that folds it into a
`Msg` must be exhaustive.

## `request`

```ipe
request : a -> Decoder b -> Task b
```

`request cmd decoder` — a correlated one-shot request/reply over the port.

The ergonomic bridge between a browser one-shot operation (geolocation fix,
clipboard read, a bespoke JS call) and a `Task Error a` in the Ipê program. It
removes the hand-rolled Cmd + Sub + correlation boilerplate a one-shot request
otherwise requires.

Semantics:

  1. An unpredictable, runtime-minted correlation token is drawn from the OS
     random source (never a counter, never derived from JS input); without
     that source the `Task` fails with an `Unavailable` error.
  2. `cmd` is sent outbound with the token on the wire envelope; the
     first-party JS port glue (or a developer's `ipe.onReceive` handler that
     opts in to correlation) echoes the token on the reply. Page JS sees the
     token, so it routes a reply but does not authenticate the page.
  3. The runtime routes the reply to the one-shot waiter, runs `decoder` through
     the SEALED fail-closed gate, and resolves the `Task`. The same seal codec
     the raw port uses; no trust change.
  4. A host trap / decode-miss / timeout / unknown-or-late id → typed `Err`,
     never a panic or a partial value. Bounded: a ceiling caps outstanding
     waiters, and a request past it fails at once with an `Unavailable` error
     (it frees as replies arrive); a per-waiter deadline evicts slow/missing
     replies.

`cmd` MUST be a seal-legal value type — the same discipline `send` enforces
(IPE-N0039). `Decoder Value` is REJECTED; spell the reply type concretely.

A `js_subscribe` subscriber never sees a correlated reply — correlation routing
intercepts it before the broadcast. No cross-talk between concurrent `request`
calls: each token resolves ONLY its own waiter; an unknown, duplicate, late,
or malformed token is dropped fail-closed, never broadcast.

## `openSession`

```ipe
openSession : a -> Decoder frame -> Task SessionHandle
```

`openSession openCmd frameDecoder` — open a session: send `openCmd` outbound
(with an unpredictable, runtime-minted session token on the envelope, never
derived from JS) and return the opaque handle. The handle is the ONLY way to
address the session from Ipê; the token, not the handle, names it on the wire.

`openCmd` MUST be a seal-legal value type — the same discipline `send` enforces
(IPE-N0039); a `Secret` or reserved-sink payload is REJECTED fail-closed at
compile time. `frameDecoder` fixes the inbound frame type for `sessionFrames`;
`Decoder Value` is REJECTED (spell the frame type concretely). The `Task` fails
with `Err` when the host rejects the open, and with an `Unavailable` error when
the open-session ceiling is reached (it frees as sessions close) or the OS
random source is unavailable.

## `sessionFrames`

```ipe
sessionFrames : SessionHandle -> Decoder frame -> (frame -> msg) -> Sub msg
```

`sessionFrames handle frameDecoder toMsg` — the inbound frame stream for THIS
session, routed by the session's runtime-minted token and seal-gated. `frameDecoder` IS the
security gate (the same explicit-decoder idiom `subscribe` uses): each inbound
frame runs through the total, fail-closed, bounded seal decoder; a malformed /
oversized / mismatched frame is DROPPED whole (no partial value, no panic).
`Decoder Value` is REJECTED (IPE-N0039). A `handle` for a closed/evicted session
yields an inert stream — it receives nothing, never another session's frames.

## `sendToSession`

```ipe
sendToSession : SessionHandle -> sessionCmd -> Cmd msg
```

`sendToSession handle sessionCmd` — send a control cmd (e.g. `Stop`) to THIS
session, seal-encoded and tagged with the session's token so it reaches only
this session's host operation; for a handle not held it sends nothing. `sessionCmd` MUST be a seal-legal value type
(IPE-N0039); a `Secret` or reserved-sink payload is REJECTED fail-closed.

## `closeSession`

```ipe
closeSession : SessionHandle -> closeCmd -> Decoder terminal -> Task terminal
```

`closeSession handle closeCmd terminalDecoder` — close the session: send
`closeCmd`, await the terminal reply, and evict the session token.

`closeCmd` MUST be seal-legal (IPE-N0039). The terminal reply runs through the
SEALED fail-closed gate fixed by `terminalDecoder` (`Decoder Value` REJECTED);
a host trap / decode-miss / deadline / budget-overflow resolves the `Task` with
a typed `Err`, never a panic or a partial value. After close the handle is dead:
a later `sendToSession` reaches no live host operation, and a later inbound frame
tagged with its token is dropped fail-closed.
